newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices were mixed with Confederate bond futures closing unchanged and roughly in the middle of the day's trading range.

One trader said the market was in need of a breather after recent strong gains. "Technically it looks like we are in need of a small correction," the trader said, adding that 118.20/18 could offer support on the March Confederate bond futures contract, which has set successive new highs lately.
Markets were waiting for U.S. January employment data on Friday. German jobs data showing the country's unemployment at a post-war high had little impact on Swiss bond prices.
Two borrowers increased Swiss franc foreign bond issues.
Guinness raised the amount of an offering launched Wednesday to 200 million francs from 125 million.
Sigma Finance increased to 400 million an earlier issue which has been repeatedly stocked up since the offering was launched in October. It added 100 million francs this time.
One trader said the market remained favourable for new foreign bonds, especially in the five-year area.
But investors were selective despite the fact that Swiss yields are seen as relatively low, with 10-year federal paper yielding well under 4.00 percent.
The Swiss average yield of public paper, reflecting maturities over five years which are noncallable for over three years, was at 3.62 percent Thursday, which was back near 1996 lows, traders said.
High-quality foreign issues garnered demand, including Triple A Deutsche Siedlungs- und Landesrentenbank's 3-1/4 percent 2002 franc issue, quoted at a yield of 2.87/88 percent.

Norway's state of Oppland-backed Oppland Energiverke which launched a 150 million franc bond earlier this week due in 2003, was also in demand, traders said. It was quoted by one bank yielding 3.33 percent.
March Conf futures CONFH7 steady at 118.49.
March Comi medium-term bond COMIH7 down five at 111.50
Mar Euro Swiss francs FESH7 steady at 98.27.
